paragraphs: Friend, here's what Moses is teaching: God cares about justice, and justice means telling the difference between a heart that meant harm and a heart that didn't. The man whose axe blade flew off the handle did not intend any harm, so Moses gives him a city to run to (Deuteronomy 19:4-6). The man who hated his neighbor and lay in wait gets no such shelter (Deuteronomy 19:11-13). Same death, two very different hearts, and God sees the difference every single time.

Now watch what Moses does with the courtroom. One lone witness is not enough, because a matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses (Deuteronomy 19:15). And if a witness lies, the judges must investigate thoroughly, and it all happens in the presence of the LORD (Deuteronomy 19:17-18). I love this, because it means nobody gets to ruin a neighbor with one big mouth and a good story. Moses even says that when the people hear about it, they will be afraid and not do such evil again (Deuteronomy 19:20).

So what does this mean for you, baker? Truth matters, and so does mercy, and God cares about both of them at the same time. Moses says not to move your neighbor's boundary marker (Deuteronomy 19:14), and the courtroom rules guard a neighbor from a lying mouth (Deuteronomy 19:15-19), so how you treat the people around you is worth taking seriously. Be careful with your words, be slow to assume the worst, and I'll be over here trying not to swing my axe at anything.
